evidence: product-price.validator.ts: ProductPriceValidator.addRules flags `this.subject.props.price.getValue() <= 0` as 'Price must be greater than 0'.

product-status.validator.ts: ProductStatusValidator.addRules re-checks `status === ProductStatus.ACTIVE && this.subject.props.price.getValue() === 0`. This repeats the price-positive rule and puts a price rule inside the status validator.

product-business-rules.validator.ts: ProductBusinessRulesValidator.addRules is the dedicated home for cross-field rules (price vs nameLength * 10000, descriptionLength vs nameLength), but the status/price cross-field rule lives elsewhere.

product-business-rules.validator.ts: the comment says '1000 veces' but the code uses `nameLength * 10000`. The method also calls name/description getValue() without the null checks done in product-name.validator.ts and product-description.validator.ts.
All five classes extend AbstractRuleValidator<Product> and use addBrokenRule, so they use the abstraction consistently.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All five files cover one concern: validating the Product aggregate. Each one extends AbstractRuleValidator<Product> and reports problems through addBrokenRule, so the module uses its own abstraction consistently.

The problem is where the rules live. The rule that a price can't be zero is enforced in two places. ProductPriceValidator already flags any price <= 0. ProductStatusValidator checks the same thing again with `status === ProductStatus.ACTIVE && price.getValue() === 0`. That second check can never catch anything the price validator misses.

Cross-field business rules are also split between two files. ProductBusinessRulesValidator exists to hold them: price compared with name length, and description length compared with name length. Yet ProductStatusValidator carries its own status-versus-price rule. Because these rules are spread out instead of kept in one place, the rubric's "keep each rule or invariant in one place" condition fails.

There are also smaller problems. ProductBusinessRulesValidator's comment says the limit is "1000 veces" but the code uses 10000. It also calls `props.description.getValue()` and `props.name.getValue()` without the null checks that ProductNameValidator and ProductDescriptionValidator do, so it quietly depends on those validators running first.

violations.message: ProductStatusValidator.addRules repeats the price rule (`price.getValue() === 0` for ACTIVE), which ProductPriceValidator already covers with `<= 0`. It also holds a cross-field business rule that belongs in ProductBusinessRulesValidator, so this rule is not kept in one place.

ProductBusinessRulesValidator is meant to hold all the cross-field rules, but only has some of them (the status/price rule is in ProductStatusValidator). Its comment ('1000 veces') doesn't match the code (10000). It also dereferences name/description without the null checks done by the name and description validators.
